v2_design_match.detail: Plan faithfully implements multi-perspective v2 final design: (1) 3-window prior-return stratification (5d/20d/60d) as demanded by Red-Team round 2, (2) upside-shock placebo leveraging K7, (3) large-cap subset re-run leveraging K4/K9. Step 4 (continuous regression with prior_ret control) is the agreed robustness supplement from idea #2. All four steps match the final question text in multi_perspective_round2.md.

pass_criteria.detail: Primary criterion (prior-up group retains CAR<0 in >=2 of 3 windows, p<0.10) and secondary criterion (upside-shock turnover effect non-significant, p>0.10) are clearly stated with both_required=true. Fail criteria mirror them exactly. The 2-of-3 majority rule for the 3-window test is a sensible robustness threshold.
minor_notes: Plan does not specify one-sided vs two-sided tests. Recommend documenting this in implementation (two-sided for primary, one-sided for placebo) but not blocking.

performance.detail: Reuses Q05 pre-computed car_20d_mat matrix approach, adds turnover_mat. No bootstrap required (direct group comparison + t-tests + OLS). With ~45 event days x ~200 stocks, stratified cells have ~1,100-2,250 obs. Runtime under 2 minutes. No concern.

minor_notes: Stratifying turnover-high into prior-up/prior-down halves each cell to ~1,100 obs (full) or ~550 obs (large-cap). Power may be tight for large-cap prior-up subgroup at p<0.10. The continuous regression in Step 4 mitigates this detection power risk.

Multiple testing across 3 windows x 2 shock directions x 2 size cuts = 12 hypothesis tests. The 2-of-3 majority rule partially addresses this but no formal correction (Bonferroni/BH) is mentioned. Acceptable for exploratory research; should be noted in the final report.

additional_observations: Data flow correctly reuses Q03 downward-shock panel builder, avoiding redundant code.

Step 3 (upside placebo) is the strongest identification element. If upside-shock turnover effect is significant, the entire turnover narrative (K7, K9, K12) would need revision. Plan correctly treats this as a hard fail.
Plan does not include DiD-style comparison for turnover (analogous to Q05 for vol). This is intentional: Q06 addresses momentum-vs-panic, not shock-specificity. A turnover DiD is deferred if needed.
recommendations: Document one-sided vs two-sided test choice in implementation comments.
Note absence of formal multiple-testing correction in the final knowledge entry.
Monitor large-cap prior-up subgroup sample size; if n<300, flag reduced power in results JSON.
summary: Plan is well-aligned with multi-perspective v2 design. All four steps (3-window stratification, large-cap re-run, upside placebo, continuous regression) match the agreed specification. Pass/fail criteria are clear and actionable. No performance concerns. Two minor statistical notes (subgroup power for large-cap prior-up, no formal multiple-testing correction) are non-blocking given the exploratory context and continuous-regression backup. Approved for implementation.
